claims.text: The newly added max_processes constructor parameter is missing from the class's :param documentation block.

Dead method _create_process_for_shard is defined but never called - _ensure_processes_alive calls _create_process_for_shards directly with the process_index and its shard list, making this a refactoring leftover that should be removed

spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy is now incremented once per shard owned by an unhealthy process instead of once per unhealthy-process event, inflating the counter by a factor of shard-count and breaking the semantics existing dashboards/alerts assume.

Remove the unused `_create_process_for_shard` method or document if it's reserved for future use. The method at lines 127-132 has no callers in the codebase and only delegates to `_create_process_for_shards`. If not intended for public API or future extension, it should be removed to reduce maintenance burden.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

spans.buffer.max-flush-segments effectively changes meaning from a global per-flush cap to a per-process cap: since each SpansBuffer now only sees 1/N of the shards, flush_segments' ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) formula results in an aggregate cap across N processes of roughly N × max_flush_segments instead of the original single value.

The class docstring's new claim "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing" only holds when max_processes is None; the actually deployed process-spans consumer uses the CLI default of 1 (one process for all shards), so the docstring describes the opposite of the real default deployment behavior.
After scaling --flusher-processes to N, Kafka producer and Redis connection counts roughly multiply by N; does the target cluster have headroom for that, and what value of N is actually planned?
_create_process_for_shard (singular, line 127) is defined but never called anywhere - it's dead code that should be removed

SpanFlusher's constructor requires a full SpansBuffer argument but only ever reads its assigned_shards attribute before discarding it and building N new SpansBuffer instances internally, meaning the signature demands more than the class actually needs and the passed-in buffer creates an extra unused Redis connection in the parent process.

SpanFlusher's class-level default behavior changed: previously max_processes unset meant one process total; now `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means unset defaults to one process per shard — the highest-resource-usage option — while the CLI default is still pinned to 1, so the two defaults point in opposite directions and any new caller that doesn't set max_processes explicitly could unknowingly spawn many processes.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts bookkeeping fields (process counts, shard-to-process map size) that are trivially true from the constructor logic, but never asserts that the produced `messages` list actually contains all expected segments — so the real risk of this change, whether shards split across multiple processes still get fully flushed without loss or duplication, is completely uncovered, and the heavily-modified _ensure_processes_alive has no test touching it at all (which is why F-001 isn't caught by tests).
Are the two modified tests in test_consumer.py stable in CI, given they now depend on real threads and Redis and one of them has a no-op'd time.sleep turning the flusher thread into a busy loop?
The CLAUDE.md edit leaves an extra blank line before the code fence that wasn't there prior to this change.
process.kill() in _ensure_processes_alive is a regression since the pre-PR code called it unconditionally, meaning unhealthy/hung processes are now never killed before spawning a replacement
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
Having both _create_process_for_shard and _create_process_for_shards methods with near-identical names is confusing for future maintainers
--flusher-processes accepts negative integers which can make SpanFlusher.num_processes invalid and crash shard-to-process mapping/modulo at startup - should enforce minimum of 1

The diff adds a hasattr/isinstance Python convention example to CLAUDE.md that is unrelated to the span buffer multiprocess change, making it harder to trace via git log why/when that convention was added if bundled into this PR.

submit()'s Redis memory check now queries the entire cluster-wide INFO once per SpansBuffer (i.e. once per flusher process) instead of once total, redundantly repeating the same cluster-wide query N times per submit call (though the resulting used/available ratio itself remains correct, and this code path is skipped entirely at the default max-memory-percentage=1.0).
default=1 for flusher_processes forces the flusher back to a single process. Should leave unset so the existing SpanFlusher default can scale to the assigned shard count.
Inconsistent metric tagging with 'shard' and 'shards'

The `if not process: continue` guard at the start of _ensure_processes_alive can never be true, since self.processes only ever holds SpawnProcess or threading.Thread objects (neither defines __bool__/__len__) and is never populated with None.
Fixed sleep in tests can be flaky; wait on condition instead

The new shard_tag used in metrics has unbounded cardinality: it's a comma-joined string of the shards a process owns, which changes on every Kafka rebalance and combination of --flusher-processes, so metrics like spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes (fired per segment) can produce an unbounded number of distinct tag values.

The new --flusher-processes CLI flag has no lower-bound validation: passing 0 falls back (due to Python falsy-0 behavior in `max_processes or len(...)`) to "one process per shard", the opposite of what a user passing 0 likely intends and the highest resource usage option; passing a negative value crashes with an opaque KeyError instead of a clear parameter error.

_create_process_for_shard (singular) is dead code with no callers anywhere in the repo, and its name misleadingly suggests a "restart just one shard" capability that doesn't actually exist (it would restart the whole process, interrupting other shards on it too).
